untuned_candidates.title: DBSCAN eps parameter too small in embed_atoms.py
untuned_candidates.body: Current eps value produces only 5 clusters from 854 atoms (844 singletons/noise) vs. prior 25+ clusters. Atoms linked by 20+ references fail to cluster. Tuning eps upward needed; current value treats similar atoms as noise instead of forming meaningful groups.

untuned_candidates.title: Incremental atom clustering re-computes all cluster IDs
untuned_candidates.body: cluster-atoms re-runs full DBSCAN, resetting cluster_ids for all 854 atoms and overwriting prior assignments. Breaks concurrent harvest workflows—adding ~30 new atoms nulls ~850 old cluster pointers. Needs incremental DBSCAN variant or post-harvest reconciliation pass.

untuned_candidates.title: DBSCAN eps threshold on normalized vectors
untuned_candidates.body: On L2-normalized embeddings, Euclidean eps relates to cosine similarity via: cos_sim = 1 - eps²/2. eps=0.36 yields cos_sim=0.935 floor, catching only near-paraphrases. Explains why original tuning failed to produce thematic clusters: DBSCAN threshold was mathematically too tight for semantic grouping.

untuned_candidates.title: Concurrent ID generation race condition
untuned_candidates.body: add_atom.py, add_cluster.py, add_source.py, migrate_atoms.py all use unguarded SELECT MAX(id)+1. Under concurrent sessions (normal case when multiple /harvest-knowledge runs overlap), two processes read same MAX(id) before either commits, causing primary-key collision. Blocks the new constraint: multiple simultaneous sessions writing atoms.

untuned_candidates.title: Incremental clustering loop architecture
untuned_candidates.body: Proper flow: (1) cache embeddings persistently, (2) match new atoms to existing centroids, (3) run DBSCAN only on orphans, (4) re-sweep all atoms against new + existing centroids. Unifies blind embed_atoms.py DBSCAN with reconcile_vault.py centroid-matching. Creates new clusters only when orphans can't fit existing centroids.

untuned_candidates.title: sqlite-vec for embedding cache with agent ANN access
untuned_candidates.body: Chose sqlite-vec vec0 virtual table over plain BLOB column to enable agent-facing ANN/cosine search, not just internal caching. Eliminates per-run Ollama cost (only new/edited atoms re-embed). Future agents can query atoms semantically via native vec0 queries.

untuned_candidates.title: Curated related-links and embedding signals are independent
untuned_candidates.body: The `related:` field is LLM-curated at atom-creation time; raw embedding cosine distance is a separate semantic signal. No inherent correlation — explains why atoms with 20 curated related-links didn't land in same DBSCAN cluster as those links. Two different signals, no reason to expect agreement.

untuned_candidates.title: Backlog has ~3 duplicate clusters per concept

Results: 3x '8-Phase Memory Write ___', 3x 'Async ... Fan-Out', 3x 'Token Budget ___', 3x 'Parallel Agent .../Git Worktree'. Root cause: add_cluster.py upserts by exact name-string match only; no semantic dedup across runs.

untuned_candidates.title: Auto-apply atoms above confidence threshold
untuned_candidates.body: Design: new atoms matching existing clusters above confidence threshold auto-apply (fast path); below threshold or no match require review before assignment. Balances automation speed with audit trail for edge cases.

untuned_candidates.title: BEGIN IMMEDIATE for ID lock, embedding outside transaction
untuned_candidates.body: Concurrent writes to atoms.db must lock only during ID allocation (BEGIN IMMEDIATE); perform embedding outside the transaction to avoid serializing writers behind Ollama latency. Discovered real concurrent-write collision risk in 4 legacy atoms scripts; pattern prevents stalls.

untuned_candidates.title: Best-of-N similarity inflates false positives
untuned_candidates.body: Selecting best match from large candidate set (800+) causes artificial score inflation even for non-duplicates due to extreme-value statistics. Threshold designed for low-risk additions (0.75) falsely approves high-risk deletions; use separate, stricter threshold for destructive decisions.

untuned_candidates.title: High-risk-only testing strategy
untuned_candidates.body: Test only operations with genuine branching/complexity: centroid math, threshold bands, concurrent ID ops, cache hit/miss. Skip CLI/glob/writer/glue (boilerplate rarely breaks). Keeps suite focused, reduces noise.

untuned_candidates.title: Concurrent ID allocation via write_txn prevents collision
untuned_candidates.body: Use database transaction lock (`id_alloc.write_txn()`) to serialize concurrent add_atom/cluster/source operations. Real threads + contention validated; prevents IntegrityError and duplicate ID assignment.

untuned_candidates.title: Similarity thresholds fail for shared-vocabulary domains
untuned_candidates.body: When domain vocabulary is highly shared (e.g., all atoms about agents/workflows), similarity scores saturate across the range even for genuinely distinct concepts. Tested: 0.878 threshold produced 29 false positives and 1 false negative; real duplicates (0.83–1.0) and noise (0.80–0.92) ranges overlap completely with no clean separator. No pure-similarity cutoff works at any threshold value for deduplication decisions.

untuned_candidates.title: Direct membership is zero-error deduplication signal
untuned_candidates.body: For clustering deduplication: atoms literally appearing in both clusters (shared_members field) provides the only deterministic signal. Zero false positives, zero false negatives across 663 candidate pairs. Similarity scoring creates noise; direct set membership creates certainty. Use for auto-merge decisions when this evidence is available.

untuned_candidates.title: Transitive merges via hub nodes over-merge unrelated clusters
untuned_candidates.body: Building transitive merge groups: if a hub cluster legitimately touches multiple distinct topics, transitively merging all connected clusters creates false mega-merges. Example: 'Agent Role Archetype' touches 'context loading', 'permission schema', 'role archetypes' — these are distinct, not duplicates. Fix: identify true cliques (every pairwise combination directly evidenced), reject hub-mediated chains. Of 23 merge candidates, 21 were cliques; 2 were invalid transitive chains.

untuned_candidates.title: Destructive actions require direct user authorization
untuned_candidates.body: Agents must refuse destructive operations (content deletion/merging) based on coordinator-relayed claims of user approval. Coordinator messages—even detailed and pre-computed—don't constitute user authorization. Only direct user messages grant escalation for destructive actions. This prevents coordinators from triggering irreversible changes mid-task.

untuned_candidates.title: Case-sensitive DB names orphan rows on case-insensitive filesystems
untuned_candidates.body: On Windows (case-insensitive filesystem): DB rows with case-only-different names (e.g., 'Phase-level Rollback' vs 'Phase-Level Rollback') point to the same physical file. Whichever row is written last wins on disk, leaving earlier DB rows orphaned with no corresponding file. Audit for case-only duplicates when merging.
